answer: No. When installing with Installation Manager (which is used for Omnibus 8.1 fixpacks), IBM explicitly recommends that you do not use paths that include symbolic links for the agent data directory, Installation Manager binaries, shared resources directory, or product installation directories. Installation Manager stores these paths as absolute paths with symbolic links resolved, and if the symbolic links change, Installation Manager might fail to start or be unable to update or uninstall products. (Note: separate guidance exists for creating symbolic links to specific library files on AIX after applying a fix pack, but this does not apply to the installation directory paths themselves.)

IBM Installation Manager must not be installed on an NFS or network-mounted disk (such as the Ingram Server mount). The documentation explicitly states to only install Installation Manager on a local disk, as network mounts cause issues including failure to delete JRE folders during uninstall and application errors like the Eclipse ProgressMonitorDialog error you are seeing. If Installation Manager is using paths that no longer exist after remounting, create the old paths manually and mount the affected file systems at the original locations used by Installation Manager, ensuring the user IDs have read access to each level of the recreated paths.

These errors indicate that the temporary directory for extension points has become corrupted, which can happen after a server is upgraded. To resolve: 1) Stop the WebSphere_Portal server, 2) Delete the contents of <wp_profile root>/temp/<node name>/WebSphere_Portal/_extensionregistry, 3) Start the WebSphere_Portal server.

To change the maximum string length for a property in ACCE, follow these steps to modify the property definition: 1. Launch ACCE. 2. Expand the object stores folder and click the object store to open the Object Store tab. 3. Expand the Data Design folder and Classes folder, then click the document class to open the Document Class tab. 4. From the Properties tab, open the Property Definitions drop down and select the property definition you want to modify. 5. ACCE will open that property definition in a new Properties tab. 6. Modify the property definition as required (including the maximum string length). 7. Go back to the Class Definition tab and click Save.

Create a siebel.properties file in the classpath of the adapter (for example, <adapter project>\connectorModule) and set the property siebel.conmgr.txtimeout to a value higher than the default 600000 milliseconds (10 minutes) to accommodate the processing time for large orders. Then restart the adapter and broker to pick up the settings. The error SBL-JCA-317 indicates the request was abandoned after the default transaction timeout of approximately 600000 ms was exceeded.

To move all IBM P8 Content Platform Engine (CPE) logs—including p8_server_error.log, p8_server_trace.log, pesvr_system.log, pesvr_trace.log, the GCD folder, pedata folders, and other related files—out of the default location, add the system property 'user.dir' to the JVM arguments of the WebSphere Application Server. The documentation does not specify the exact precision granularity of the backside persistent timeout value. However, it explains that intermittent 'Failed to process response headers' errors can occur even when DataPower's persistent timeout (28s) is lower than the backend's (30s) because the error is also caused by failed connection attempts on reused persistent connections that have already been closed by something outside of DataPower (such as the backend device closing the connection), or by a broad range of network errors—not solely by timeout expiration. A packet trace and debug-level logs are recommended to confirm the specific cause. As a workaround, lowering the DataPower persistent timeout further or disabling persistent connections may help prevent the problem.

In Atlas 6.0.3.3, the Atlas Extensions logging configuration has moved to the log4j.properties file. To configure it: 1) Navigate to <Atlas_Install_folder>/Atlas/Properties folder. 2) Edit the log4.properties file. 3) Update the path information for the following three properties: log4j.appender.MATTER_APPENDER.File=matter_adapter.log, log4j.appender.PERSON_APPENDER.File=person_adapter.log, and log4j.appender.ORG_UNIT_APPENDER.File=org_unit_adapter.log. 4) Save the file. 5) Restart the Atlas application server.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21993043. The bulletin states that WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus are affected by an Open Source Apache Tomcat vulnerability (CVE-2016-3092). Apache Tomcat is vulnerable to a denial of service caused by an error in the Apache Commons FileUpload component; by sending file upload requests, an attacker could cause the server to become unresponsive. The CVSS Base Score is 5.3 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L). The current temporal score can be found at the IBM X-Force Exchange link provided in the bulletin.

The information is available in IBM Security Bulletin swg21968399. The bulletin states that the Telemetry (MQXR) service can be configured to use SSL/TLS connections, and the passphrase used to access the keystore is written to the file system in clear text in a world-readable properties file. CVE-2015-2012 describes that IBM WebSphere MQ stores the MQXR keystore password in clear text in a world readable file. CVSS Base Score is 2.1 (Vector: AV:L/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N). Affected versions are IBM WebSphere MQ 8.0 (8.0.0.3 and earlier), 7.5 (7.5.0.5 and earlier), and 7.1 (7.1.0.6 and earlier). Remediation: install fixpack 8.0.0.4 for MQ 8.0, apply interim fix IT09866 for MQ 7.5, and install fixpack 7.1.0.7 for MQ 7.1.

Yes. IBM Tivoli Log File Agent Version 6.3.0 Fix Pack 02 (6.3.0-TIV-ITM_LFA-FP0002) adds support for a Windows x86-64 bit (WIX64) Log File agent. The documentation also recommends using the Windows (WIX64) x86-64 bit Log File agent to minimize certain issues, and notes that before installing the LO x86-64 bit agent you must uninstall the WINNT 32-bit version of the agent and the 32/64-bit compatibility package.

The use of the Client Channel Definition Table (CCDT) with XA connections is not supported. This restriction exists because of transaction recovery: if the application server stops while there are still active transactions, there is no way with the current implementation to ensure that it will connect to the same queue manager when it restarts, which can lead to in-doubt transactions being left dangling and never resolved. When attempting to create an XA connection from WAS to MQ using a connection factory that uses a CCDT, you may see error MQJMS1068: failed to obtain XAResource. Use direct connections (such as jms/QM01 and jms/QM02) for XA/MDB listeners instead of the CCDT-based QCF.

The retrieved documentation (swg27045339) confirms that Liberty added support for IBM WebSphere SDK Java Technology Edition 8.0 in fix pack 5, but the specific minimum supported RHEL operating system levels are not visible in the provided excerpt. The excerpt only lists AIX minimums (AIX 6.1 TL7 and AIX 7.1 TL3). Based solely on the available context, support for RHEL 5.8 and RHEL 5.11 with Java 8.0 cannot be confirmed.

The information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21975233: 'Vulnerability in MD5 Signature and Hash Algorithm affects WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus (CVE-2015-7575)'. The bulletin describes the MD5 'SLOTH' vulnerability on TLS 1.2 where the TLS protocol could allow weaker than expected security caused by a collision attack when using the MD5 hash function for signing a ServerKeyExchange message during a TLS handshake. An attacker could exploit this using man-in-the-middle techniques to impersonate a TLS server and obtain credentials. CVSS Base Score is 7.1. Affected products include IBM Integration Bus V9 and V10 (and Toolkit), and WebSphere Message Broker V7 and V8 (and Toolkit). Remediation is available via APARs: IT07823 and IT07802 for IIB V10 (available in fix pack 10.0.0.1), IT07823 for IIB V9 (interim fix from IBM Fix Central), and IT09602 for WMB V8 (interim fix from IBM Fix Central, targeted for fix pack 8.0.0.7). IBM recommends avoiding ciphers which use an MD5 or SHA-1 signature hash.

The information is contained in IBM Security Bulletin swg22014367. The bulletin details CVE-2017-3735, a vulnerability in OpenSSL where an error parsing an IPAddressFamily extension in an X.509 certificate could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information via an out-of-bounds read (CVSS Base Score 4.3, Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N). It lists all versions of WebSphere MQ 5.3 and MQ 8 for HPE NonStop Server as affected, provides remediation links via IBM Fix Central for MQ 5.3.1.14 and MQ 8, and notes no workarounds are available. Note: The change history indicates a correction on 29 March 2018 to remove HPE NonStop as an affected platform.
The reason is that the 'S-TAP Approval Needed' option is checked in the S-TAP Certification screen on the Appliance. To resolve this, uncheck the Approval box and the S-TAPs should start connecting.

The information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21995004. The WebAdmin context for WebSphere Message Broker Version 8 allows directory listings (CVE-2016-6080), which could disclose sensitive information to an attacker. CVSS Base Score is 5.3 (Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N). The affected product is WebSphere Message Broker V8. The fix is available via APAR IT16698 in Fix Pack 8.0.0.8 (https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24042925). No workarounds or mitigations are listed. For unsupported versions, IBM recommends upgrading to a fixed, supported version.

These messages are false errors that can occur on the IBM WebSphere DataPower M/T 9235 appliance and do not affect appliance operation. To confirm the power supplies are working normally, check the LED status on the power supplies; if the LEDs are green, the power supplies are working normally. To recover from the false errors, perform a reboot of the appliance. From the WebGUI: Control Panel → System Control → In the 'Shutdown' section choose 'Reboot System' then click 'Shutdown'. From the CLI: enter 'top', then 'shutdown reboot', then 'y'. In most cases, the reboot resets the sensors and no additional errors are logged. If the issue reoccurs on the same appliance, contact IBM DataPower support with the number of occurrences and the outputs of: show clock, show version, show ipmi, show sensors-other, config, service show, and test hardware.

The unusually small war and ear files are caused by the CDPATH operating system environment variable being set. The create_web_client_war.sh script contains a change directory (cd) command to include the WorkplaceXT directory in the archive, but when CDPATH is set, the cd command may jump to unintended directories and fail with the error "create_web_client_war.sh[5]: cd: .WorkplaceXT: [No such file or directory]". To resolve this, unset the CDPATH environment variable while creating the IBM FileNet Workplace XT war and ear files.

The information is available in IBM Security Bulletin swg21998655, titled 'IBM Security Bulletin: Malicious File Download vulnerability in IBM Business Process Manager (BPM) and WebSphere Lombardi Edition (WLE) - CVE-2016-9693'. The bulletin describes a CSV download feature available to anonymous users that allows an attacker to craft a URL triggering download of attacker-supplied content under an attacker-supplied file name (CVE-2016-9693, CVSS Base Score 7.1). Affected versions include WebSphere Lombardi Edition V7.2.0.0 - V7.2.0.5, IBM BPM Advanced V7.5.0.0 - V7.5.1.2, V8.0.0.0 - V8.0.1.3, and V8.5.0.0 - V8.5.7.0 including cumulative fix 2016.12. Remediation is to install interim fix JR57149. For IBM BPM V7.5 and WLE (out of general support), customers with a support extension contract can contact IBM support; the fix disables the vulnerable URL and uses HTML5 features to trigger CSV download without server interaction.

No, JazzSM does not support HTTP access. By default, the Jazz for Service Management application server requires HTTPS access. Although you can technically set up the environment for both HTTP and HTTPS by editing the web.xml files, HTTP access is explicitly not supported for security reasons.

The cause is that changes made to the setCenteraLibPath.sh or setCenteraLibPath.bat file were not picked up by the WebSphere Application Server startup script. This typically occurs when the WAS Content Engine instance is restarted from within the WAS console rather than from the command line, so the setCenteraLibPath.sh file (even if added to setupcmdLine.sh) is not recognized. As a result, the CenteraSDK path is not loaded and the FPLibrary is not found in java.library.path, causing the fixed content provider initialization to fail.

When upgrading a BigFix server, most of the time is usually spent upgrading the database. During this phase, the installer launches the BESAdmin utility but does not provide detailed progress, so the upgrade may appear hung or not progressing (on Windows, the BESAdmin UI may indicate 'Not Responding' if clicked; on Linux, the message 'Info: Configuring the database for the server component, please wait ...' is reported). It is important to allow the upgrade to complete in this state and not attempt to cancel or kill the upgrade process. To verify the upgrade is still active, check that the relevant process is still running.

No. According to the documentation, the HTTP CONNECT method is used specifically for SSL tunneling (SSL proxy requests) when using a Multi-Protocol Gateway. For non-SSL proxy requests, DataPower does not use the CONNECT method; instead, non-SSL requests are proxied using standard methods such as 'GET hostname:port/URI' via an XML Firewall (HTTP Options tab) or a Multi-Protocol Gateway (HTTP Proxy Policy in the User Agent).

No. According to the documentation, in WebSphere Application Server 8.5.5.x and below, the EJBDeploy tool can only deploy Java EE applications compiled with a JDK level of 7 or below. To deploy JDK 8 compiled applications using EJBDeploy, you must upgrade to WebSphere Application Server V9 or later.

This information is published in the IBM Security Bulletin titled "IBM Security Bulletin: IBM MQ Appliance is affected by a Network Security Services (NSS) vulnerability (CVE-2017-5461)" (Technote swg22005055, with related updates in swg22003852, swg22009796, and swg22009842). The bulletin describes CVE-2017-5461 as an out-of-bounds write during Base64 decoding in the NSS library (CVSS Base Score 8.8), affecting IBM MQ Appliance 8.0 (maintenance levels 8.0.0.0 through 8.0.0.7) and 9.0.x Continuous Delivery releases 9.0.1 through 9.0.3. Remediation is to apply fixpack 8.0.0.8 for the 8.0 line or upgrade to Continuous Delivery Release 9.0.4 for the 9.0.x CD line; no workarounds or mitigations are available. The bulletin is available via IBM Support/Technote and the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal.

wpcollector is a command line tool that automates the collection of portal logs and configuration files. It is delivered with WebSphere Portal beginning with the 7.0 release. Using automated log collection early in the Case life cycle can greatly reduce the number of doc requests that are made by Support. When run, it creates a wp.mustgather-<timestamp>.zip file in the <wp_profile_root>/filesForAutoPD/ directory.

If DLTLICPGM LICPGM(5724C04) fails to uninstall the ITM i5/OS agent, perform the following manual steps on the IBM i system:

1. DLTLIB QAUTOMON
2. DLTLIB QAUTOTMP
3. DLTUSRPRF QAUTOMON and choose to remove all objects owned by this user
4. Start QSH: start qsh
5. In QSH, delete the agent directories and all subdirectories:
   - delete /QIBM/USERDATA/IBM/ITM
   - delete /QIBM/PRODDATA/IBM/ITM
6. After completing these steps, retry the RSTLICPGM command to reinstall the newer release as specified in the user guide.

By default, Solaris does not write verbose GC output to a log file; it must be explicitly configured. For WAS 8.5.0.2+, 8.0.0.6+, or 7.0.0.27+ on Solaris, add the following to the generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails, -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps, -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC, and -Xloggc:/tmp/gc.log (replace /tmp/gc.log with your desired path). To enable log rotation, also add -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation, -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10, and -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M. Note that -Xverbosegc alone writes to native_stdout; use -Xloggc:<fileName> to direct output to a file.

Beginning in firmware version 6.0 and above, the default SSL settings changed: Crypto profiles now enable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 by default. This affects the protocol version included in the Client Hello when DataPower acts as the SSL client. Some legacy servers with non-compliant SSL implementations may reject connection attempts when TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.1 are used, causing the handshake to fail without negotiating to a mutually agreeable protocol. To resolve, upgrade the SSL server to a version compliant with SSL/TLS specifications, or disable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 within the Crypto Profile (navigate to Objects > Crypto Configuration > Crypto Profile, select your specific profile, and view the Options selection to see supported SSL protocol versions).

When searching for a string that contains a reserved character such as "-", you need to escape it by placing a backslash ("\") in front of the character. For example, to search for "String1-String2", you should enter "String1\-String2". Please refer to the Oracle documentation for Special Characters in Oracle Text Queries for additional details.

To permanently resolve this error, apply WebSphere Portal 8.5.0.0 Combined Cumulative Fix 05 (PI31198) or later, which contains a code fix for this issue. As a local workaround, open the WAS admin console, navigate to Resources > Resource environment providers > WP ScriptingService > Custom properties, delete the entry named "ServerExt.applications" with value "com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions", save, and restart the server. Alternatively, if the temporary extension registry directory is corrupted (often after an upgrade), stop the WebSphere_Portal server, delete the contents of <wp_profile root>/temp/<node name>/WebSphere_Portal/_extensionregistry, and restart the server.

Affected WebSphere Enterprise Service Bus versions are 6.2, 7.0, and 7.5. The 'Too many open files' error indicates the process has exhausted its file handle limit (including sockets), typically caused by system configuration limits being too low or by file descriptor leaks in the application. To diagnose, display the current soft limit with `ulimit -Sn` and hard limit with `ulimit -Hn`, or capture a Javacore using `kill -3 PID` (the limit appears under NOFILE). To resolve, increase the limit using `ulimit -n [value]`; a value of 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime, though this depends on your specific file/socket usage. Note that ulimit changes only take effect after restarting the application server and nodeagent on the same command line where the ulimit command was executed. On Linux, setting the limit to 'unlimited' may not be permitted on certain Red Hat Enterprise Linux versions (e.g., RHEL 5 has a maximum of 1048576). If the error persists even with a high limit, check for file descriptor leaks using the `lsof` command to identify open files and sockets.

The cause of these errors is that the 'S-TAP Approval Needed' option is checked in the S-TAP Certification screen on the Guardium Appliance. To resolve this, uncheck the Approval box and the S-TAPs should start connecting and appear in S-TAP Control.

The ABEND S013 in PARMGEN job KCIJPALO is caused by the MQ Configuration (KMC) component not being included in OMEGAMON for Messaging V7.5.00. The V7.5 Serverpac does not install the MQ Configuration FMIDs (HKMC730 and HKCF730), but if the component remains selected in your PARMGEN LPAR runtime environment (RTE), it can cause unexpected results such as the S013 abend during allocation. To resolve, deselect 'KMC OMEGAMON for Messaging – WebSphere MQ Configuration' from the 'Include Products in this PARMGEN RTE panel (KCIP@PGI)' under step '1 KCIJPCFG Set-up/Refresh PARMGEN work environment' so it is removed from the RTE during reconfiguration/upgrade.

Yes. By default, when an SCA module is uninstalled (including during an update), its associated destinations are removed even if there are still messages in the destination queue, so messages on internal SCA queues would be deleted. To prevent message loss during production updates, set the SCA.recycleDestinations custom JVM property for the module to false to preserve the SCA destinations.

The HTTP Session time-out for a Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server can be set in the following locations, listed from lowest to highest precedence:

1. **Server Level** (Administrative Console): Navigate to Servers > Application Servers > Your Server > Web Container > Session Management. Select 'Set time-out' and enter the value in minutes. This is the lowest precedence level.

2. **Enterprise Application Level** (Administrative Console): Navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Session Management. Check 'Override' in the Override Session Management section, then set the time-out value. This overrides the Server Level setting if Override is selected.

3. **Web Application Level** (Administrative Console): Overrides both Server and Enterprise Application settings if Override is selected.

4. **Application Level (web.xml)**: Set at packaging time in the web.xml file using <session-config><session-timeout>value</session-timeout></session-config> (value in minutes). This overrides all Administrative Console settings.

5. **Application Code**: Using the setMaxInactiveInterval() method on the HttpSession object. This overrides all other settings including web.xml and Administrative Console configurations.

To increase the time-out, modify the appropriate level according to your needs, keeping in mind that higher precedence settings (especially application code and web.xml) will override lower-level Administrative Console settings.

The information is available in IBM Security Bulletin swg21959745. The bulletin states that the Logjam Attack (CVE-2015-4000) on TLS connections using Diffie-Hellman key exchange affects all versions of IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-thru (MQIPT) prior to 2.1.0.2. The vulnerability allows a remote attacker to use man-in-the-middle techniques to force a downgrade to 512-bit export-grade cipher, potentially recovering the session key and modifying traffic (CVSS Base Score 4.3). Remediation requires upgrading to MQIPT 2.1.0.2 (SupportPac MS81); no workarounds are available.

No, you should not upgrade to Oracle JDK 8. IBM Mobile Foundation, IBM Worklight, IBM Worklight Foundation, and IBM MobileFirst Platform Foundation support Oracle JDK 7 but do not support Oracle JDK 8. If you have already migrated to Oracle JDK 8 (which may happen automatically on Windows and Mac OS), you must revert to Oracle JDK 7 by uninstalling Oracle JDK 8 and reinstalling the latest version of Oracle JDK 7.

Yes. To prevent internal SCA queues (destinations) from being deleted and recreated when updating/uninstalling an SCA module, set the custom JVM property SCA.recycleDestinations to false for the module. This preserves the SCA destinations and any messages still on them.

In CMOD v9.0 on Windows, server trace files are written in binary format and must be converted using the ARSTFMT command located in the CMOD\9.0\bin directory. To format the trace: open a command prompt, navigate to the CMOD\9.0\bin directory, and run: arstfmt -i <path_to_unreadable_trace_file> -o <path_to_output_file.txt>, where the -i parameter specifies the binary trace file and the -o parameter specifies the name of the formatted text output file.

This is expected behavior due to Defect 138519. In this patch (FP10/IF0001), the name of the default SQL Server instance was changed from HOSTNAME to MSSQLSERVER. Previously, the default instance was configured with the hostname, but now it is identified as 'MSSQLSERVER'. If you previously configured the default instance using the hostname, you must unconfigure that instance and reconfigure it using the name 'MSSQLSERVER'. To do this: 1) Open Manage Tivoli Enterprise Monitoring Services (MTEMS), 2) Right-click the template row and select 'Configure Using Defaults', 3) Select the default instance with name HOSTNAME from 'Server To Monitor' and click '>>' to unconfigure it, 4) Select the instance named 'MSSQLSERVER' in 'Database Servers Available' and click '<<' to configure it, 5) Set configuration parameters and start the agent.

This VerifyError ('Inaccessible class' for org/apache/http/HttpEntity) is a known side effect of interim fix PI50993. According to the technote, after applying PI50993, the API in HTTPCore and HTTPClient libraries are no longer visible to applications, which can cause NoClassDefFoundError or VerifyError. To resolve this, the application must be updated to bundle the HTTPCore and HTTPClient libraries with the application itself.

The details are documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21985017. CVE-2016-2961 describes that IBM Integration Bus uses Apache Tomcat to serve HTTP requests for HTTPInput and SOAPInput nodes, and an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a malformed HTTP POST request to the integration server HTTP listener to obtain a Java stack trace revealing the Apache Tomcat version. CVSS Base Score is 5.3 (Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N). Affected products are IBM Integration Bus V10.0 and V9.0, and WebSphere Message Broker V8.0. Remediation is via APAR IT15188: available in IBM Integration Bus fix pack 10.0.0.5, an interim fix from IBM Fix Central for IIB V9, targeted for WebSphere Message Broker fix pack 9.0.0.6, and targeted for WMB 8.0.0.8. For unsupported versions, upgrade to a fixed supported version is recommended.
